evidence.name: Presumptive Color Test Results
evidence.description: Three suspected drug samples were recovered from the residence and subjected to presumptive color tests at the scene. Each sample produced a distinct blue coloration when treated with the Scott reagent, a reaction consistent with the presence of cocaine. A parallel Marquis reagent test on the same samples produced no color change, which is an expected and consistent finding for cocaine, as cocaine typically does not react with the Marquis reagent. These presumptive results are preliminary and were later confirmed through instrumental analysis.
truth_base: one field test with the scott reagent showed a color change indicating a possible positive result for cocaine (player may describe this as a reagent turning blue, a positive reaction, or similar; exact scott reagent name not required)

a field test with the marquis reagent showed no reaction, and the player understands this does not contradict the first test but is actually expected for cocaine (any phrasing conveying that a lack of color change is still consistent with cocaine is acceptable; exact marquis reagent name not required)

the player conveys that these on-scene tests are only preliminary/presumptive and cannot confirm the drug's identity on their own, requiring further lab confirmation (words like 'not conclusive', 'needs to be confirmed', or 'just a screening test' all count)

evidence.name: GC-MS Confirmatory Analysis
evidence.description: Following solid phase extraction to isolate and purify the compound from each sample, all three prepared samples were analyzed using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry. Each sample's chromatogram displayed a major peak whose relative retention time matched a laboratory-certified cocaine reference standard analyzed under the same instrumental conditions. The mass spectra generated for each evidence sample were also compared against the reference standard's spectrum and found to be consistent. Net and gross weights of each sample were recorded prior to analysis: the net weight represents the mass of the pure powder extracted from each bag, while the gross weight represents the mass of the entire sealed evidence bag as received.
truth_base: the sample was purified in a liquid form before running it through the instrument (any mention of an extraction, purification, or preparation step counts, exact technique name like 'solid phase extraction' not required)

the timing or pattern of the sample's peak on the chromatogram lined up with a known cocaine reference sample tested the same way (player may describe this loosely as 'it matched the reference' or 'came out at the same time/spot')

the chemical spectrum produced by the sample matched the reference standard's spectrum (any phrasing indicating the two spectra looked the same or matched is sufficient; mass spectrum and chromatogram wording is not necessary)

the player mentions that both the small sample weight and the weight of the whole sealed bags were measured and recorded (does not need to use the terms 'net' or 'gross', just needs to convey two separate weighings happened)
the player conveys that this lab-based result confirmed or backed up the earlier presumptive field test, giving a definite identification of the drug

evidence.name: Cyanoacrylate Fuming of Firearm
evidence.description: A firearm recovered from the scene was processed for latent fingerprints using cyanoacrylate (superglue) fuming. The firearm was placed in a sealed chamber along with heated superglue and distilled water to generate cyanoacrylate vapors, which bond to the amino acids, fatty acids, and other residues present in latent fingerprints, developing them into a visible white polymer ridge pattern on the firearm's surface. This method was selected because it is effective on non-porous surfaces such as metal, and it preserves the developed print for photography and further comparison without disturbing the ridge detail.
truth_base: a fuming/vapor-based method involving glue was used to develop the print (does not need the exact term 'cyanoacrylate', 'superglue fuming' or a general description of a chamber/vapor process is enough)
the player mentions that this method works well on surfaces like metal, which is why it suited a firearm (any comparison to it being unsuitable for something like paper/porous material also counts)

the process makes the print visible without damaging or smudging the ridge pattern, so it can be photographed/compared afterward (phrasing like 'it doesn't destroy the print' or 'preserves the detail' is sufficient)

evidence.name: AFIS Comparison of Developed Print
evidence.description: The latent print developed on the firearm was photographed and imported into the Automated Fingerprint Identification System for comparison against records on file. The system returned a candidate match with a comparison score of 70, which was used as the basis for a manual ridge-by-ridge examination by the examiner. AFIS is used to narrow down a large database to a short list of likely candidates, but the final identification determination is always made by a qualified fingerprint examiner conducting a point-by-point comparison, not by the automated system alone.
truth_base: the developed print was run through an automated fingerprint database/system to search for possible matches (does not need the acronym 'AFIS' specifically, describing a database search or computer comparison system is enough)

the player conveys that the automated system only narrows things down to likely candidates or gives a score, rather than making a final call by itself (any phrasing like 'it just suggests matches' or 'gives a shortlist' counts)

a human examiner still had to manually review and compare the print point-by-point to actually confirm the identification (phrasing like 'a person had to check it themselves' or 'manually verified' is sufficient, exact terminology not required)
